status_summary: Executive Order 14154 (signed 2025-01-20) restarted reviews of LNG export applications and directed expanded energy development, Executive Order 14156 (same day) declared a national energy emergency, and Executive Order 14213 (signed 2025-02-14) created a National Energy Dominance Council chaired by the Interior Secretary with State, Trade Representative and Defense seats. DOE reported on 2025-10-22 that it had authorized more than 13.8 billion cubic feet a day of LNG exports under this administration, and the August 2025 U.S.-EU framework statement records an expected EU offtake of US energy valued at $750 billion through 2028. Interior held the third of the Gulf of America lease sales required by law on 2026-08-12 ($82.7 million in high bids). The overseas dimension rests mostly on trade commitments and export approvals; the Foreword's wider aims of geopolitical leverage and reindustrialization are not measurable in the sources read.

timeline.event: President signs Executive Order 14154, Unleashing American Energy: it expands energy development on federal lands and waters, restarts DOE reviews of LNG export applications (section 8), pauses disbursement of Inflation Reduction Act and Infrastructure Act funds and tasks agencies with international mineral competitiveness work. It creates no enforceable rights.
President signs Executive Order 14156 declaring a national energy emergency (published 2025-01-29), citing inadequate energy production, transportation, refining and generation.

President signs Executive Order 14213 (published 2025-02-20) establishing the National Energy Dominance Council, chaired by the Interior Secretary, to advise on expanding energy production and exports and to recommend a National Energy Dominance Strategy; it sets no specific international program.
U.S.-EU joint statement on a trade framework records an expected EU offtake of US liquefied natural gas, oil and nuclear energy products valued at $750 billion through 2028.

DOE issues the final non-FTA export authorization for Venture Global's CP2 LNG project (up to 3.96 Bcf/d) and states that it has authorized more than 13.8 Bcf/d of LNG exports under this administration, with U.S. exports at about 15 Bcf/d.

Interior announces results of the third Gulf of America lease sale required under the 2025 reconciliation law: $82.7 million in high bids on 59 blocks from 16 companies, at a 12.5 percent royalty rate.

title: Go on offense on energy: assert US oil and gas interests and pursue dominance
uncertainties: The Foreword sets no end state, so the implemented stage reflects operative domestic and export measures rather than a measurable global outcome. The DOE figure of 13.8 Bcf/d is DOE's own claim and was not independently verified. The Executive Order 14156 page was read via its Federal Register summary; the order's link to the national emergency authorities was not analyzed. The EU statement records an expectation, and actual purchases were not checked. Foreign policy steps that assert energy interests abroad (sanctions, diplomatic actions on Russia, Iran or Venezuela) were not examined in this record. Chapter 12 and 16 records c12-04, c16-01 and c16-03 carry detail on LNG and leasing. In review, implemented was kept because the domestic production, leasing and export measures are operative in substance; the Foreword's goal is broad and the geopolitical outcomes it names are not measured, which is why progress is held at the bottom of the implemented band.
